Q: Python command/event registration pattern A:

You can have it happen at "import time" by implementing the registration behavior in each submodule's __init__.py file.

Please note that the submodules will not be automatically "discovered" upon program initialization, and the registration for each submodule's handler will only happen if that submodule is imported at all during program startup/execution. To tackle this, you may, for instance:

  • import all necessary submodules during the program's "main", so to speak -- this gives you extremely granular control of what handlers will be available at runtime, but leaves the door open for mistakes due to leaving a handler behind, or including a handler that no longer exists;
  • use a utility such as pkgutil.iter_modules to automatically discover all available handlers.

Q: How do you go about setting up a virtual IP address? A:

A Virtual IP address is a secondary IP set on a host, it's just another IP bound to an adapter (adapters if bonded). This IP is useful for many things but most commonly used for webservers to run multiple SSL certificates for multiple sites.

In CentOS you pretty much copy the /etc/sysconfig/network-scripts/ifcfg-eth0 (whichever for the adapter you want) to /etc/sysconfig/network-scripts/ifcfg-eth0:1, In there change the devicename=eth0 to devicename=eth0:1 and change the IP for the new "virtual IP" you want.
